note: Claim ledger. Each claim names a profile, one evidence tier, an artifact that exists, the profile fields it depends on and a standing. A claim that depends on a field tagged tier4-community, tier5-emulator-hint, inference or unknown-default-chosen is provisional. Vocabulary: docs/evidence-tiers.md.

claims.statement: On the CP-1600 manual's reading, a push writes the word at the address held in R6 and then increments R6, and a pull first decrements R6 and then reads, so the stack grows toward higher addresses.
claims.note: The expectation comes from three manual pages read in plan 01-02 (C17 resolved-primary). Applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP-1610 is an inference logged as C31 in the discrepancy log, so the claim stays provisional.

claims.statement: The NTSC STIC part of this profile is the AY-3-8900-1, operated from a 3.579545 MHz crystal.
claims.note: All three fields carry tier1-primary-doc tags citing the 1980 data catalog; the page was a research-era reading and is re-read when the profile is next revised. The claim states only the printed figure; the exact crystal ratio is logged as C9. The STIC1A variant is not modelled.

claims.statement: A nominal NTSC frame is 262 scanlines times 57 CPU cycles, which is 14,934 CPU cycles and 59,736 master ticks.
claims.note: The scanline and per-scanline counts are tier4-community and the ticks per CPU cycle are an inference, so the weakest-field rule makes the claim provisional. A primary source or a measurement would resolve it.

claims.statement: The CP-1600 manual marks shifts and the instructions EIS, DIS, TCI, CLRC and SETC as not interruptible and says nothing about HLT, SDBD and MVO.
claims.note: This records what the manual pages say (C19 partial). Whether the silent cases are interruptible on the CP1610 is unresolved, and applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP1610 is an inference logged as C31.

claims.statement: Every one of the 1024 10-bit opcode decle patterns maps to exactly one most-specific row of the CP-1610 family table, with one documented coincidence (0010 111 111: TSTR R7, JR R7 and MOVR R7,R7).
claims.note: The table is transcribed from the CP-1600 manual page images and the coverage check proves the rows tile the decle space, not that any encoding, cycle count or status bit was read correctly. Applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP1610 is an inference logged as C31, so the claim stays provisional.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, the read and write widths of every address, the mirror extents of RAM and ROM rows and the behaviour-changing row boundaries, observed through the real bus functions, together with the device, impl and gate labels (and stub mirror labels) reported by the introspection function, equal the structural columns of the sourced literal map.
claims.note: Evidence: case memmap.dump.matches-literal of suite memmap writes the decode dump of all 65,536 addresses in both views, and the memmap gate step compares the dev and release dumps with the literal (plan 03-06). A pass shows transcription consistency between the literal map and the runtime decode, not hardware truth. Widths, RAM and ROM mirrors and the boundaries where they change are behavioural; the device, impl and gate columns and the mirror of stub and undriven rows are declarative labels from ivs_memsys_describe. Several depended-on fields are tier4-community, inference or unknown-default-chosen (C5, C11, C20, C21, C60, C61, C62), so the claim is provisional; a D10 decode probe on owner hardware would raise it.

claims.statement: The core's IVSC v1 layer-1 parser accepts every positive record and refuses every malformed record of fixture FX-ivsc-vectors with the status, reason, segment index and byte offset that docs/formats/ivsc-v1.md documents for it, and the seeded fuzz family of suite ivsc reaches every refusal reason of that specification without breaking the parser's refusal, determinism and round-trip invariants.
claims.note: Evidence: suite ivsc in the dev (ASan and UBSan) and release presets, with the parse-level records of data/cart/ivsc-parse.json and the fuzz family ivsc.fuzz.* (eight fixed seeds and ivsc.fuzz.reasons-covered, plan 03-08); six named faults in data/expected/faults/ivsc.ids show that the fixtures catch the loss of a parser rule. The expectations come from the project's own specification, and every positive trailer and whole-file digest was computed with cmake -E sha256sum, independently of the core's SHA-256. IVSC is the project's own format, so this is conformance to the project specification, not to any hardware or third-party format. Layer 1 knows no profile; the claim names the profile whose cartridge fields admit IVSC v1. cartridge.slots is unknown-default-chosen (a scope choice), so the weakest-field rule makes the claim provisional. The layer-2 load into an instance is not covered here (plan 03-11).
